text: The gut microbiome is hard to study mainly because it is not one thing but a very large community of bacteria, fungi and viruses that live together. Each person carry a different mix, and even in the same person the mix change from day to day, depending on what we eat, our sleep, stress and the medicine we take. Because of this, when scientists compare two groups, it is difficult to know if the difference comes from the microbes or from many other factors in the life of the people. Another problem is that most studies are done on mice or in a dish, and these results do not always transfer to real humans. The methods to measure the bacteria also are not fully standard, so two labs can get different answer from the same sample. What this means for health claims is that we should be careful. When a product says it "fixes your gut" or a food will "boost good bacteria", often the evidence is weak or only from small studies. The science is still young, so in my opinion the honest position is to stay curious but not believe every strong claim, especially when someone is trying to sell something.
